sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_factor.name: Zoom Amount
sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_factor.tooltip: How much the camera zooms in while the zoom key (by default: C, in the Miscellaneous category under Controls) is active. OptiFine uses 4x by default.
sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_mode.name: Zoom Mode
sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_mode.tooltip: "Hold" zooms only while the zoom key is pressed down."Toggle" presses once to zoom and again to stop.
sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_smooth.name: Smooth Zoom
sodiumlegacy.options.zoom_smooth.tooltip: If enabled, the camera zoom will animate in and out smoothly instead of instantly switching between the zoomed and un-zoomed view.
sodiumlegacy.options.translucent_culling: Removes the interior faces between adjacent identical translucent blocks (glass, stained glass, ice...), so they render as one seamless body instead of showing seams. Basic OptiFine "connected textures" support.
Glass and stained glass connect seamlessly (textures are generated automatically), and resource packs with OptiFine/MCPatcher connected-texture rules are supported. Needs a resource reload (F3 + T) to apply.
sodiumlegacy.options.view_distance.toolt: The render distance controls how far away terrain will be rendered. Shorter distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates.
sodiumlegacy.options.simulation_distance: The simulation distance controls how far away terrain and entities will be loaded and ticked. Shorter distances can reduce the internal server's load and may improve frame rates.
sodiumlegacy.options.brightness.tooltip: Controls the brightness (gamma) of the game.
sodiumlegacy.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scale factor to be used for the user interface. If "auto" is used, then the largest scale factor will always be used.
sodiumlegacy.options.fullscreen.tooltip: If enabled, the game will display in full-screen (if supported).
sodiumlegacy.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game's frame rate will be synchronized to the monitor's refresh rate, making for a generally smoother experience at the expense of overall input latency. This setting might reduce performance if your system is too slow.
sodiumlegacy.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limits the maximum number of frames per second. This can help reduce battery usage and system load when multi-tasking. If VSync is enabled, this option will be ignored unless it is lower than your display's refresh rate.
sodiumlegacy.options.view_bobbing.toolti: If enabled, the player's view will sway and bob when moving around. Players who experience motion sickness while playing may benefit from disabling this.
sodiumlegacy.options.attack_indicator.to: Controls where the Attack Indicator is displayed on screen.
If enabled, an indicator will be shown when the game is saving the world to disk.
sodiumlegacy.options.graphics_quality.to: Controls the overall graphics quality of the game (Fast or Fancy). Other quality options set to "Default" will follow this setting.
sodiumlegacy.options.clouds_quality.tool: The quality level used for rendering clouds in the sky. Even though the options are labeled "Fast" and "Fancy", the effect on performance is negligible.
sodiumlegacy.options.weather_quality.too: Controls the distance that weather effects, such as rain and snow, will be rendered.
sodiumlegacy.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodiumlegacy.options.leaves_quality.tool: Controls whether leaves will be rendered as transparent (fancy) or opaque (fast).
sodiumlegacy.options.dynamic_lights.name: Dynamic Lights
sodiumlegacy.options.dynamic_lights.tool: Blocks that emit light (torches, glowstone...) light up their surroundings while held by a player or dropped on the ground. Fast updates every 0.5 s, Fancy updates every tick. Costs chunk rebuilds while the light moves.
sodiumlegacy.options.particles.tooltip: Controls whether "%s" particles are shown. Disabled particles are never created at all, which can improve frame rates in busy scenes.
sodiumlegacy.options.particles.lava.name: Lava Sparks
sodiumlegacy.options.particles.note.name: Notes
sodiumlegacy.options.particles.crit.name: Critical Hits
sodiumlegacy.options.particles.snow.name: Snowball / Snow
sodiumlegacy.options.smooth_lighting.too: Enables the smooth lighting and shading of blocks in the world. This can very slightly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update a chunk, but it doesn't affect frame rates.
sodiumlegacy.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The distance (in blocks) which biome colors are smoothly blended across. Using higher values will greatly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update chunks, for diminishing improvements in quality.
sodiumlegacy.options.entity_distance.too: The render distance multiplier used by entity rendering. Smaller values decrease, and larger values increase, the maximum distance at which entities will be rendered.
sodiumlegacy.options.entity_shadows.tool: If enabled, basic shadows will be rendered beneath mobs and other entities.
sodiumlegacy.options.mipmap_type.name: Mipmap Type
sodiumlegacy.options.mipmap_type.tooltip: Controls how block textures are filtered in the distance (only has an effect when Mipmap Levels is above 0). Nearest and Linear keep the sharp, pixelated vanilla look. Bilinear and Trilinear smooth distant textures, but at high mipmap levels colors of neighbouring textures can bleed slightly into each other.
sodiumlegacy.options.anisotropic_filteri: Keeps block textures sharp when seen at a shallow angle, such as the ground stretching into the distance. Higher values look better with a small performance cost on weaker GPUs. Limited by what your graphics card supports.
sodiumlegacy.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodiumlegacy.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be applied when the player is in darker areas, which makes the overall image darker and more dramatic.
sodiumlegacy.options.mipmap_levels.toolt: Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but could adversely affect performance with resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodiumlegacy.options.use_block_face_cull: If enabled, only the faces of blocks which are facing the camera will be submitted for rendering. This can eliminate a large number of block faces very early in the rendering process, which greatly improves rendering performance. Some resource packs may have issues with this option, so try disabling it if you're seeing holes in blocks.
sodiumlegacy.options.use_fog_occlusion.t: If enabled, chunks which are determined to be fully hidden by fog effects will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The improvement can be more dramatic when fog effects are heavier (such as while underwater), but it may cause undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some scenarios.
If enabled, entities which are within the camera viewport, but not inside of a visible chunk, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization uses the visibility data which already exists for chunk rendering and does not add overhead.
sodiumlegacy.options.animate_only_visibl: If enabled, only the animated textures which are determined to be visible in the current image will be updated. This can provide a significant performance improvement on some hardware, especially with heavier resource packs. If you experience issues with some textures not being animated, try disabling this option.
sodiumlegacy.options.cpu_render_ahead_li: For debugging only. Specifies the maximum number of frames which can be in-flight to the GPU. Changing this value is not recommended, as very low or high values may create frame rate instability.
sodiumlegacy.options.use_persistent_mapp:
For debugging only. If enabled, persistent memory mappings will be used for the staging buffer so that unnecessary memory copies can be avoided. Disabling this can be useful for narrowing down the cause of graphical corruption.

Requires OpenGL 4.4 or ARB_buffer_storage.
sodiumlegacy.options.chunk_update_thread: Specifies the number of threads to use for chunk building. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and update speed, but may negatively impact frame times. The default value is usually good enough for all situations.
sodiumlegacy.options.always_defer_chunk_: If enabled, rendering will never wait for chunk updates to finish, even if they are important. This can greatly improve frame rates in some scenarios, but it may create significant visual lag where blocks take a while to appear or disappear.
